## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]

## 9. All 30 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] CPU: ColdFire MCF54415CMJ250 (chip marking read 2026-09-30): MCF5441x, V4 core with EMAC, 250 MHz, no separate DSP. All audio is ColdFire assembly. It is the same CPU family as Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1, Rytm and A4; the Octatrack is the exception. The MCF54418 reference manual applies. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#454f0b95` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L9) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [hw] Audio: 6 tracks, rendered per 32-sample block (0.67 ms) in the audio interrupt. The stock OS already takes about 77 % of each block, even when stopped, because all tracks and effects are computed every block. Peaks reach 99 % with heavy added engines. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#f6da9f46` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L10) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [doc] [hw] The startup menu lives in flash that OS updates never write. Hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE, "READY TO RECEIVE". It listens to MIDI IN only, never USB. — `model-cycles-samples#b3624cd5` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L15) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Model:Cycles' MIDI IN is a 3.5 mm TRS jack (type A and B both work). A mono TS cable does not work. Use the supplied DIN adapter if your interface has DIN. — `model-cycles-samples#ddb912c6` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:16](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L16) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Takes 5-10 minutes; the unit restarts by itself. — `model-cycles-samples#2bce129e` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:17](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L17) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [hw] If it stays on "RECEIVING..." a packet was lost: power cycle and send slower (Modded Cycles' flasher pace 1.4 by default, 2.0 when it fails). `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#26b97ccc` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L18) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Free space is scarce. The project's main source of code room is freed sprite masks: Groups of byte-identical `0xFF` bitmap masks are each referenced by one 32-bit constant. Redirecting that constant to a kept copy renders identically and frees the others. 10 groups, 164 freeable masks, 104-1,024 bytes each. Never write into a kept copy. A registry tool tracks which mod owns which mask. — `model-cycles-samples#1e5faa84` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L40) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
- [doc] [hw] Other `0xFF` caves are refused when stock code points into them. — `model-cycles-samples#969e69f4` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:44](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L44) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
- [emu] [hw] Every stock voice is rendered every block, playing or not: about 7,600 instructions each, so six idle voices cost ~45,800 per block. Stock audio takes ~77 % of the CPU at rest, measured on a unit with a diagnostic load counter (the same figure as in Modded-Cycles' notes). Skipping silent voices cut 77 % of the voice-loop instructions in the emulator; the unit test is still open. `[hw]` / `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#a78e5c78` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L51) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)

- [hw] Thresholds seen on units: the sound crackles when a block nears 100 % of its time; a single block at 91 % did *not* crackle; the UI was still fluid at ~86 % sustained load and slows above that. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#f8c82655` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L62) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
- [hw] Mistake 1: reacting to one heavy block. Peaks are isolated: a step where several tracks start (the sequencer takes up to ~7 % of a block), or caches the UI flushed between blocks (+4.6 points). By the time the governor sees such a block, it is already over; cutting a voice can't rescue it and is audible. The fix reacts only to a peak that lasts two blocks, or to sustained load. On a unit: "works well", 6 tracks with effects at 89 % peak / 78 % average, no crackle. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#d97619cf` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:68](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L68) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
- [hw] A sample in use is locked. Once a track uses a sample, the Model:Cycles refuses to delete it; a restart unlocks it only if no track uses it anymore (tried on a Model:Cycles with one SAMPLE track, 2026-11-10). An uploader should delete what it can and name the locked files rather than stop. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#a6780cfd` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:85](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L85) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / The +Drive sample store (model27's sample uploader, OS 1.13)
- [emu] Stock voices start accumulating into ACC0 without clearing it, so they rely on an empty accumulator at entry. Leave ACC0 at 0 (as on the Syntakt). `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#cce8680a` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:54](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L54) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
- [emu] USB multitrack glitches (reported on Reddit after 15-20 minutes): Cause: the OS sends each block to USB right after rendering it, and the 6-channel mod's queue tolerated only 0.2 ms of jitter. With variable engine load (muted tracks, effects off) frames went missing. Fix: send at a fixed time at the start of the next interrupt, align the queue at start-up, and use a 9-slot ring instead of 8. Zero defects in the simulator afterwards. General rule for USB streaming mods: decouple the send time from a variable render time. `[emu]` (cause read in the OS, fix simulated) — `model-cycles-samples#e0c972d2` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L55) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
- [emu] Mistake 2: an integer moving average that never moves. `slow += (load - slow) >> 8` with load and average in whole percent rounds every step to 0, or to -1 below the average. The "sustained load" rule therefore never fired on a unit. The emulator test hid it because it pre-set the average. Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units (e.g. load << 8), and test them from a cold start. `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#a5c5bf10` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:72](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L72) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
- [emu] EMAC wrappers are not free: wrapping the reverb kernels in helpers that saved ACC3 and MACSR around every product cost +20-48 % instructions. Save the EMAC state once per block. `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#8726bdbe` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L77) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)

- [doc] Container: ELE3, text header plus section table (16-byte aligned), with a trailer of zero padding, 4 zero bytes and an HMAC-SHA256 at a 16-byte-aligned offset.
